groups.defect: When the unified-storage call fails in Create (line 45) and Update (line 129), the duration is recorded with recordLegacyDuration when it should use recordStorageDuration.
groups.rationale: Every member reports the same copy-paste metric mix-up on the storage-failure path. It appears in both Create and Update, and each spot needs its own edit.

groups.defect: The legacy DeleteCollection goroutine records its latency with recordStorageDuration when it should use recordLegacyDuration.
groups.rationale: All four point at line 166 and describe the same wrong metric helper.

groups.defect: In Delete, the success metric passes the object name as the kind label (line 106), which mislabels the series and creates unbounded cardinality. Line 97 also puts the plain d.Log into the context instead of the enriched log.
groups.rationale: s_6b11a209 reports both Delete defects, so it links the line-106 name-label group with the line-97 logger group.

groups.defect: The async legacy-write goroutines build their context from the request context, so the writes are cancelled when the handler returns and fail without any log. This affects Create, Delete, Update and DeleteCollection.
groups.rationale: All three report the same request-context cancellation problem with the same fix (context.WithoutCancel plus logging), and each one already lists every affected method.

groups.defect: Update passes the raw objInfo to the legacy update instead of an updateWrapper around the storage result. Legacy then recomputes the object, which can diverge from the unified copy, and UpdatedObject is called twice. Async writes can also be applied to legacy out of order.
groups.rationale: All three report that removing updateWrapper lets the two stores diverge. s_4d3c3dc5 also raises the ordering problem.

groups.defect: Delete now returns early on a NotFound from unified storage and no longer falls through to the legacy delete, so objects that exist only in legacy can never be deleted.
groups.rationale: Both describe the same lost IsNotFound fallback in Delete.

groups.defect: The Mode3 tests never wait for or assert the async legacy writes. The Delete and DeleteCollection tests do not even register legacy expectations, so the legacy write path is unverified.
groups.rationale: s_a1fd1880 covers the Delete/DeleteCollection part of the broader gap that s_6e8d049a describes for all Mode3 tests.
